title: git-vouch-attest: verify FIDO attestations (separate tool)
description: Separate executable per METARULE 2. Stdlib Python; all crypto via the openssl CLI. Input: a person file key's attestation {blob, challenge} (or files) plus a user-supplied vendor root (--ca FILE); no bundled roots. Steps: parse ssh-sk-attest-v01 blob, verify the attestation signature over authData||SHA-256(challenge) with the cert key (openssl), confirm the credential public key in authData matches the SSH key, verify the cert chain to --ca (openssl verify). Packed format first; fido-u2f optional.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-validated against OpenSSH regress/misc/ssh-verify-attestation (built from ~/GIT/openssh-portable) on the same inputs; fixture = a real hardware attestation supplied by Mark (until then, tests using a self-generated chain prove parsing/sig/key-match; chain-to-vendor test pending fixture). Tampered blob/challenge/key all rejected.
notes:
Implemented git-vouch-attest + tests/attest. Reference ssh-verify-attestation built offline: git archive of ~/GIT/openssh-portable 26b1363 into scratch, autoreconf && ./configure, make libssh.a openbsd-compat; make ssh-verify-attestation with a local fido.h declaring the 14 fido_cred_* prototypes, LIBFIDO2=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libfido2.so.1. Set SSH_VERIFY_ATTESTATION= to run the cross-check tests.
Review round 1 fixed (uncommitted): chain check now 'openssl verify -no-CApath -no-CAstore -CAfile' (system store/SSL_CERT_DIR no longer trusted; test added); openssl's verify reason passed through; AAGUID read from cert DER by a small TLV walker (asn1parse text parsing removed: UTF-8 crash + line forgery); openssl output decoded errors=replace; new fixtures/cases with reference verdicts: wrong-application, no-AT, key-type-mismatch, aaguid-mismatch, aaguid-malformed; every reject case asserts its stderr reason. 41 pass on 3.12 and 3.9 with reference binary; ruff clean; mutation run kills rpid/at/typematch/aaguid/self/no-store/reason.
Remaining: (1) real hardware fixture + vendor root from Mark (acceptance criterion). (2) OPEN QUESTION for Mark: at which time should the chain be validated - now (current), the key's 'added' date (-attime), or no time check (-no_check_time)? A stored attestation fails once the vendor cert expires.
